stem.en:
Describe a friend who is quite different from you.

You should say:
- who this friend is
- how you became friends
- in what ways you are different
and explain why you get on well in spite of these differences.

After your talk: Do you think good friends need to have the same hobbies?

Part 3 discussion:
1. Do people usually choose friends who are similar to them? Why?
2. What can you learn from a friend who thinks differently from you?
3. Can friendships that exist only online be as strong as face-to-face ones?
4. How do friendships change as people get older?

why.en: Give two clear contrasts ('she loves…, but I prefer…'), then one moment when your differences helped you both.
why.uz: Oraningizdagi ikkita aniq farqni ayting («she loves…, but I prefer…»), soʻng shu farqlar ikkalangizga ham foyda bergan bir voqeani aytib bering.
why.ru: Приведите два чётких противопоставления («she loves…, but I prefer…»), затем расскажите об одном случае, когда то, что вы такие разные, помогло вам обоим.

stem.en:
Describe a person in your neighbourhood whose work you find interesting.

You should say:
- who this person is
- where they work
- what a typical working day is like for them
and explain why you find their work interesting.

After your talk: Would you like to do this kind of work one day?

Part 3 discussion:
1. Which jobs do teenagers in your country find most interesting?
2. Should young people try a part-time job while they are still at school? Why or why not?
3. Why are some useful jobs not respected as much as others?
4. How might jobs like this change in the future?

why.en: Describe the work as if you were watching it: what the person does first, next and last. Clear steps give you plenty to say.

why.ru: Опишите работу так, будто наблюдаете за ней: что человек делает сначала, потом и в конце. Чёткие шаги дают много материала для рассказа.

Describe a classmate who is very good at something.

You should say:
- who this classmate is
- what they are good at
- when you first noticed it
and explain how you feel about their talent.

Describe a place where you can concentrate well on your studies.

- what you can see and hear there

- where it is
- what you usually buy there

Describe a place in your country that you have only seen in photos or videos.

You should say:

- where you saw photos or videos of it

Describe something you do to calm down when you feel stressed.

You should say:
- what usually makes you feel stressed
- what you do to calm down
- how you discovered it
and explain why it works for you.

After your talk: Do your friends calm down in the same way?

Part 3 discussion:
1. What makes students feel stressed these days?
2. Is it better to relax alone or with other people? Why?
3. Should schools give students more time to rest during the day?
4. Do older people and young people relax in different ways?

why.en: Contrast how you feel before and after it. Two clear pictures, 'stressed' and 'calm', make the 'why' easy to explain.
why.uz: Shu ishdan oldin va keyin oʻzingizni qanday his qilishingizni solishtiring. «stressed» va «calm» degan ikki aniq holat «nega» qismini tushuntirishni osonlashtiradi.
why.ru: Сравните, как вы себя чувствуете до и после. Две чёткие картины — «stressed» и «calm» — помогут объяснить, почему это работает.

stem.en:
Describe a habit that helps you to use your time well.

You should say:
- what the habit is
- how you started it
- what a normal day with this habit looks like
and explain what has changed since you started it.

After your talk: Do you think you waste time on anything?

Part 3 discussion:
1. Why do so many people say they do not have enough time?
2. Is it better to plan every hour of the day or to stay flexible?
3. Should parents control how teenagers spend their free time?
4. Do phones help people to manage their time, or do they make it harder?

why.en: Give one example of a real day, from morning to evening. A concrete day shows the habit better than general words like 'useful'.
why.uz: Ertalabdan kechgacha boʻlgan bitta haqiqiy kunni misol qilib keltiring. Aniq kun odatni «useful» kabi umumiy soʻzlardan koʻra yaxshiroq koʻrsatadi.
why.ru: Опишите один реальный день с утра до вечера. Конкретный пример покажет привычку лучше общих слов вроде «useful».

stem.en:
Describe a club or an activity that you think your school should start.

You should say:
- what it is
- who would run it
- how often it would meet
and explain why students need it.

After your talk: Have you ever suggested this idea to your teachers?

Part 3 discussion:
1. Should students have a say in how their school is run? Why or why not?
2. What makes a school a good place to learn?
3. Why do some people resist changes at school or at work?
4. How might schools look different in twenty years?

why.en: It does not exist yet, so use 'would' and 'could' ('it would give us…', 'we could…'), then add one example of a meeting.
why.uz: Bunday toʻgarak hali yoʻq, shuning uchun «would» va «could» ishlating («it would give us…», «we could…»), soʻng bitta mashgʻulot qanday oʻtishini misol qilib keltiring.
why.ru: Такого кружка пока нет, поэтому используйте «would» и «could» («it would give us…», «we could…»), а затем опишите, как могла бы пройти одна встреча.

stem.en:
Describe your plans for the next summer holidays.

You should say:
- what you are planning to do
- who is going to be with you
- what you need to do before then
and explain what you hope to bring back from the summer, such as a new skill or a memory.

After your talk: What did you do last summer?

Part 3 discussion:
1. How do young people in your country usually spend their summer holidays?
2. Should students study during the summer holidays or only rest? Why?
3. Are long school holidays a good idea? Why or why not?
4. How do holidays help families to spend time together?

why.en: Mix the ways of talking about the future: 'I am going to…' for plans, 'I am …ing' for arrangements, 'I hope to…' for wishes.
why.uz: Kelajak haqida turli shakllarda gapiring: rejalar uchun «I am going to…», kelishilgan ishlar uchun «I am …ing», orzular uchun «I hope to…».
why.ru: Используйте разные формы будущего: «I am going to…» для планов, «I am …ing» для договорённостей, «I hope to…» для желаний.

stem.en:
Describe a rule from your home or school that you would also have in your own home one day.

You should say:
- what the rule is
- where you have seen it work
- how you would explain it to a child
and explain why you think it is a fair rule.

After your talk: Is there a rule you would like to change?

Part 3 discussion:
1. Why do families and schools need rules?
2. Should young people help to make the rules they have to follow?
3. What should happen when someone breaks a rule at school?
4. Are rules for teenagers stricter or less strict than in the past?

why.en: Give your opinion early ('I think it is fair because…'), then support it with one example from real life and one result of the rule.
why.uz: Fikringizni boshida ayting («I think it is fair because…»), soʻng uni hayotdan bitta misol va qoidaning bitta natijasi bilan asoslang.
why.ru: Выскажите мнение в начале («I think it is fair because…»), затем подкрепите его одним примером из жизни и тем, к чему это правило приводит.

B1.en:
• Who: My friend Dilnoza is in my class, and we sit together.
• How we became friends: Our teacher put us together for a project two years ago.
• How we are different: She is loud and loves sport, but I am quiet and I prefer books.
• One moment: Once she helped me to speak in front of the class, and I helped her with her essay.
• Why we get on well: We get on well because we learn new things from each other.
• End: Our differences make our friendship more interesting.

B2.en:
• Who: The friend I'd like to describe is Dilnoza, a classmate who is almost my complete opposite.
• How we became friends: We were paired for a science project two years ago, and to my surprise we enjoyed it.
• How we are different: She is outgoing and sporty, whereas I am quite shy and happiest with a book.
• A moment that shows it: Before my first presentation in class she coached me on speaking up, and in return I helped her plan her essays.
• Why it works: What makes it work, I think, is that we balance each other out.
• Looking back: I would never have chosen her as a friend, yet she has changed me the most.

B1.en:
• Who: I want to talk about the baker on our street.
• Where she works: She works in a small bakery at the corner, next to the bus stop.
• Her day: She starts very early, bakes round bread in a big clay oven called a tandir, and sells it until lunch.
• What I notice: I pass her every morning, and the whole street smells of fresh bread.
• Why it is interesting: Her work is interesting because she makes every loaf by hand, very fast.
• End: I often stop and watch her for a minute.

B2.en:
• Who: The person I find fascinating is the baker who runs a small bakery at the corner of our street.
• Where she works: Her bakery is a tiny room with a clay oven, right next to the bus stop.
• Her day: She begins long before sunrise, pressing each round loaf onto the hot inner wall of the oven, and by lunchtime she has usually sold out.
• What stands out: What strikes me is how calm she stays, even with a queue outside.
• Why it interests me: The reason is that it looks simple, yet it clearly takes years of practice.
• Looking back: It has made me respect work we often take for granted.

• When I noticed: I only noticed it last year, when our art teacher pinned his portrait on the wall.

• My feelings: To be honest, I admire him, although at first I felt slightly jealous.
• Looking back: He has taught me that real skill comes from daily practice.

• What I work on: I tend to save my hardest tasks for that room, such as essays and maths revision.
• When I go: Saturday mornings suit me best, when the room is almost empty.
• Why it helps: The main reason it works is that nothing distracts me there, unlike at home with my younger brothers.
• Looking back: Since I started going, my homework has taken far less time.

• What we buy: Depending on the season, we pick up anything from cherries to melons, plus dried fruit in winter.
